lines.english: “Yaaawn... Ah...”

lines.japanese: 朝。定刻通りに起床。
lines.english: Morning. I woke at the appointed hour.
“Ugh, cold...”

lines.japanese: 布団にくるまって五分ほどぬくぬくしていると、これもほぼ定刻通りに、優しくドアが叩かれます。
lines.english: After I had spent five warm minutes curled beneath the covers, a gentle knock came at the door, almost exactly on schedule too.

lines.japanese: 「あの、千歳さん、おはようございます」
lines.english: “Um, good morning, Chitose.”

lines.japanese: 「ハイハイ、おはようございます小鳩さん」
lines.english: “Yes, yes. Good morning, Kobato.”

lines.japanese: 横着して寝転がったまま答えましたが、愛想だけは忘れません。
lines.english: I lazily answered without getting up, but I did remember to sound pleasant.

lines.japanese: 「朝ごはんできてるので、いつでもどうぞ」
lines.english: “Breakfast is ready, so come whenever you like.”

lines.japanese: 「うわあお、いつもありがとー、いま行きまーす」
lines.english: “Wowsers, thanks as always. Be right there.”

lines.japanese: とんとんと足音が階段を下りていきます。
lines.english: Her footsteps pattered down the stairs.

lines.japanese: ああ、起きねば。
lines.english: Ah, I had to get up.

lines.japanese: 起きて、ごはん食べて、学校へ行かねば。
lines.english: Get up, eat, and go to school.

lines.japanese: はあ、朝って辛いなあ。
lines.english: Morning was suffering.

lines.japanese: でもタカシ君は、いまの俺よりもはるかに少ない睡眠時間で、来る日も来る日もこの気だるさと戦ってたわけでしょ。偉いよなあ。
lines.english: But Takashi had fought this lethargy day after day on far less sleep than I got now, hadn't he? I had to admire him.

lines.japanese: って、もはや他人事じゃないだろ俺。
lines.english: Except this was hardly somebody else's problem anymore, was it?

lines.japanese: コンバンワ！
lines.english: GOOD EVENING!

lines.japanese: いつも元気に大声で！　朝でも夜でもコンバンワ！
lines.english: Always loud and full of pep! Morning or night, GOOD EVENING!

lines.japanese: 心の中でヨッくんの口癖を唱えながら飛びおきました。
lines.english: Chanting Yoshi's catchphrase in my mind, I sprang out of bed.

lines.japanese: 「さて！　今日もぬるっと行きますか！」
lines.english: “All right! Let’s keep it slippery today too!”

lines.japanese: 「えと、きょうは、晩ごはんどうしますか」
lines.english: “Um, what should I do about dinner tonight?”

lines.japanese: 朝食を囲みながら夕食の話をする小鳩さんは、羽田家の小さな主婦です。
lines.english: Discussing dinner over breakfast, Kobato was the Haneda household's tiny homemaker.

lines.japanese: 「そうねー、どうしようかしら……」
lines.english: “Let's see. What should we do...?”

lines.japanese: 今日はバイトが非番の日。したがって、学校が終わったあとの予定はいまのところありません。
lines.english: I had no shift at work today. That left me with no plans at present for after school.

lines.japanese: しかし、だからこそ、まっすぐ家へ帰るのももったいない気がします。
lines.english: But precisely because I was free, going straight home felt like a waste.

lines.japanese: タカシ君や隼人君と一緒になって、眩しいほどに広がった世界。最近の俺は、どんどん新しいものを見たい触れたい味わいたいのです。
lines.english: Through joining with Takashi and Hayato, the world had opened before me in dazzling breadth. Lately, I wanted to see, touch, and taste one new thing after another.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あっ、いいです、分かりました。カレーを作っとくので、もしきょう食べなかったら、あしたの朝に食べてください」
lines.english: “Oh! I-it's okay, I understand. I'll make curry, and if you don't eat it tonight, please have it tomorrow morning.”

lines.japanese: 「そう？　ごめんねえ」
lines.english: “You sure? Sorry about that.”

lines.japanese: 本当にもう小鳩さんったら気が利く良い子です。
lines.english: Honestly, Kobato was such a thoughtful, good kid.

lines.japanese: 新しい世界もいいけど、この子とももっと仲良くなって、一緒になったみんなの分まで立派なお兄ちゃんになりたいなあ、なんて思うわけです。
lines.english: The new world was wonderful, but I also wanted to grow closer to her and become a fine big brother for everyone who had joined together inside me.

lines.japanese: 「えっと……なに、なにカレーがいいですか。千歳さん、アスパラガスが苦手──」
lines.english: “Um... what kind of curry would you like? You don't like asparagus, Chitose—”

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん」
lines.english: “Big Brother.”

lines.japanese: 「へっ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃんと呼んで」
lines.english: “Call me Big Brother.”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: うわあ、迷惑そう。
lines.english: Wow, she looked bothered.

lines.japanese: 「いやほら、世間的にはボクら、兄妹なワケじゃない？」
lines.english: “I mean, to the outside world, we're brother and sister, right?”

lines.japanese: だから第三者のいる局面では、ぎくしゃくながらオニイチャンと呼んでくることもあるのですが──
lines.english: That was why, when other people were present, she sometimes awkwardly called me Big Brother—

lines.japanese: 「──外でうっかり“千歳さん”なんて呼んで余計な詮索されるのも嫌でしょ？　うちの中でもお兄ちゃんって呼んで習慣付けしといた方がいいんじゃないかしら」
lines.english: “—but you don't want to accidentally call me ‘Chitose’ in public and invite awkward questions, do you? Wouldn't it be better to get in the habit of calling me Big Brother at home too?”

lines.japanese: 「あ……はい、すいません、分かりました……」
lines.english: “Oh... Yes. Sorry. I understand...”

lines.japanese: 分かってなさそうな声で、彼女は頭を垂れました。
lines.english: She bowed her head, sounding less than convinced.

lines.japanese: でもはっきり拒絶はしないあたり、そうするべきだと思ってる部分もあるんだろうなあ。
lines.english: Still, the fact that she did not flatly refuse meant some part of her probably agreed that she ought to do it.

lines.japanese: 「や、べつに無理強いするつもりはないんだけどね」
lines.english: “I mean, I'm not trying to force you.”

lines.japanese: 美少女にお兄ちゃんと呼ばれて狂喜するような、トシローさんじみた趣味はありませんし。
lines.english: I had none of Toshirou's peculiar enthusiasm for beautiful girls calling him Big Brother.

lines.japanese: それに、分かりますよ。小鳩さんにとっての「お兄ちゃん」は、いちばん辛かったとき自分を守ってくれたヨージ君そのひとですからね。
lines.english: And I understood. To Kobato, “Big Brother” meant Youji himself, the one who had protected her through the most painful time in her life.

lines.japanese: ええ、分かるんですよ。それは。
lines.english: Yes. I understood that.

lines.japanese: 小鳩さんは長年ずっと、俺たちの特殊な事情に振りまわされてきた子ですから、学術的なことはともかく、経験則や感覚的な意味で誰よりも俺たちの事情に聡いはずです。
lines.english: For years, Kobato had been buffeted by our peculiar circumstances. Leaving the academic details aside, her experience and instincts must have given her a keener understanding of us than anyone.

lines.japanese: だからこの現状──昨日も今日も明日も、ずーっと≪千歳鷲介≫ばかり出ている現状──が、裏を返せばもう羽田ヨージは奈落から戻ってこないことだって、本当は理解しているのだと思います。
lines.english: So I thought she really understood the present situation too: yesterday, today, tomorrow, always Shuusuke Chitose and no one else. Put another way, Youji Haneda would never return from the abyss.

lines.japanese: しかし、たとえこの先もう会えないとしても、小鳩さんはかつてヨージ君という兄がいた想い出までは消したくないのでしょう。
lines.english: But even if she could never see him again, Kobato did not want to erase the memory that she had once had a brother named Youji.

lines.japanese: 幼い彼女にとって「お兄ちゃん」の座は唯一無二で、そこに他の誰かを収めることは、元の主を蹴落としてしまうことだと考えているのかもしれません。
lines.english: To a young girl like her, the place called “Big Brother” was unique. Perhaps she felt that seating anyone else there would drive out its original occupant.

lines.japanese: こっちが嬉しくなってしまうぐらい、健気で優しい妹ちゃんなのです。
lines.english: She was such a brave and tender little sister that it made me happy merely to think of her.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、そうだよね……」
lines.english: “Well, you're right...”

lines.japanese: 「ふえっ？　な、なにがですか」
lines.english: “Huh? A-about what?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、よく考えたら同じ『お兄ちゃん』だと、俺のことなのかヨージ君のことなのか紛らわしいじゃない」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, if we use the same ‘Big Brother,’ no one will know whether you mean me or Youji.”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 「だから『お兄ちゃん』って言ったらヨージ君のことで、俺のことは、そうねえ……」
lines.english: “So ‘Big Brother’ can mean Youji, and for me... Let's see...”

lines.japanese: 「『チィ兄ちゃん』なんてどう？」
lines.english: “How about ‘Big Bro Chii’?”

lines.japanese: 古き良き日本の弟・妹たちは、小さいお兄ちゃんのことをそう呼んだものです。
lines.english: Back in the good old days, that was what kids in Japan called the younger of their big brothers.

lines.japanese: 「だめ？」
lines.english: “No good?”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、いえ！　あの、それなら、ひかくてき大丈夫だと思います」
lines.english: “Oh, no! Um, I think that would be comparatively acceptable.”

lines.japanese: おっ、今度はわりと納得顔。
lines.english: Oh, she looked reasonably convinced this time.

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃんがお兄ちゃんのままなら、さつしかえはないと思います」
lines.english: “As long as Big Brother stays Big Brother, I don’t think there will be any compulcations.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。差し支えね」
lines.english: “Complications.”

lines.japanese: 「すばらしい妥協案だと思います」
lines.english: “I think it is a splendid concession.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。せめて折衷案と言おうね。チィ兄ちゃん、けっこう繊細だから」
lines.english: “Let’s at least call it a compromise. Your Big Bro Chii is a fairly sensitive man.”

lines.japanese: 「むやみになんかいな言葉を使うのは、きょうよう人ぶってるみたいで好ましくないです」
lines.english: “Using difficult words for no reason makes you sound like a pretentious intellectual. I don’t approve.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことないでしょ。現に俺、いま微笑ましい気分よ」
lines.english: “Does it? I'm certainly finding this charming.”

lines.japanese: 「千歳さんはきょうよう人じゃないから、もとから好ましいです」
lines.english: “You’re not an intellectual, Chitose, so I approve of you already.”

lines.japanese: 「えっと……誉められたのかな、俺」
lines.english: “Um... Was that a compliment?”

lines.japanese: 「むろんです」
lines.english: “Indubitably.”

lines.japanese: 「……あ、いまチィ兄ちゃんってゆうの忘れた」
lines.english: “...Oh. I forgot to call you Big Bro Chii just now.”

lines.japanese: 「まーまー。それはね、少しずつ、自然に変わってけばいいから」
lines.english: “Now, now. You can change little by little until it comes naturally.”

lines.japanese: 俺もね、そのうち君に、もっと遠慮しないでガンガン突っ込むようにしていくから。
lines.english: And in time, I would stop being so careful around her and call her out more freely, too.

lines.japanese: 及ばずながらも兄として、妹が立派な教養人になる手助けをさせてもらいますから。
lines.english: As her inadequate brother, I would do my part to help my little sister become a proper intellectual.

lines.japanese: この先、時間はいっぱいあります。お互いゆっくり歩みよっていきましょう。
lines.english: We had plenty of time ahead of us. We could take our time meeting each other halfway.

lines.japanese: 「かほうは寝て待てということわざもあります」
lines.english: “As the proverb says, good things come to those who wait.”

lines.japanese: 「ううーん、それはちょっと違うかな」
lines.english: “Mmm, not quite.”
